items.name: /distribution-vet
items.description: Maintainer-only. Classifies every file that would newly ship to adopters against the written distribution-boundary categories, withholds by default when none matches cleanly, and asks the maintainer only where the taxonomy does not settle it, so the release CLI can produce a manifest.

items.name: /gaia-cleanse
items.description: Cleanses memory and auto-loaded files (CLAUDE.md, rules) of duplication with the wiki, contradictions with the wiki, and stale content, then asks one Apply / Discuss / Decline question; on Apply it applies the report, files any out-of-scope problem as a tech-debt issue, then commits, opens a PR, and merges it on a main-branch run like /update-deps. Pass --apply to re-run the apply-and-publish stage against the most recent report. Use when the user asks to cleanse or clean up memory, CLAUDE.md, or rules for duplication, contradictions with the wiki, or stale instructions. For duplication or broken links inside the wiki itself, use /gaia-wiki instead.

items.name: /gaia-codify
items.description: Drafts a guard (deterministic check, skill, or path-scoped rule) for a recurring code-audit finding class, with approval. Reviews recurring Code Audit Team findings and drafts the lowest-context-weight form into the working tree.

items.name: /gaia-debt
items.description: Fixes the tech-debt backlog, a single issue or a recommended related batch, highest severity then oldest first, on a fresh isolated branch through the audit gate, closing the issue(s) on merge. With no argument it drains the top of the backlog; one issue number fixes that issue directly, and several issue numbers name the operator's own batch, budgeted. An optional trailing `[use] worktree|branch` picks the isolation mode. A named number that cannot be drained stops with a reason. Use when the user asks to drain, fix, or work the tech-debt backlog or a named tech-debt issue.

items.name: /gaia-fitness
items.description: Lints this project's Claude integration (skills, commands, agents, rules, hooks, settings, CLAUDE.md files, wiki) with a deterministic rule catalog and reports an F-to-A+ grade, plus Claude Code built-in results and an advisory model judgment of descriptions, trigger overlap, rule scope and terminology. Proposes fixes for project-owned files only and applies each one only on a per-file yes, then offers to publish. Use when the user asks to check, grade or tidy their Claude setup.

items.name: /gaia-forensics
items.description: Turns a GAIA workflow misfire into a redacted, classified, filing-ready bug report in one read-only pass. Self-diagnoses config issues inline and files probable bugs upstream on confirmation.

items.name: /gaia-init
items.description: Initializes a new project from the GAIA React template. Renames, strips GAIA branding, configures i18n, and installs Claude skills and plugins.

items.name: /gaia-plan
items.description: Plans a complex feature with GAIA's task-orchestration pattern, structuring the work into fresh-context subagent phases for approval. Does not implement. Use when the user asks to plan a feature, break work into phases, or turn a SPEC into an execution plan.

items.name: /gaia-release
items.description: Maintainer-only. Cuts a new GAIA release. Bumps the version, graduates the CHANGELOG, regenerates the manifest, opens the release PR, then tags on merge.

items.name: /gaia-residue
items.description: Triages the keyed audit residue recorded in merged pull-request bodies. Enumerates candidates, resolves each one's cited line, and takes one disposition per entry (promote to a tech-debt issue, dismiss, or keep). Never fixes anything.

items.name: /gaia-serena-sync
items.description: Detects the languages Serena is not indexing and, on explicit consent, additively appends them to the `language_servers:` list (`languages:` before Serena 1.7) in `.serena/project.yml`, then prompts a Serena restart. Never mutates without a yes; inert without Serena.

items.name: /gaia-spec
items.description: Authors an immutable SPEC artifact through Socratic discovery, then plans it in the same session and stops at the plan's KICKOFF prompt; execution starts in a fresh session. Pass `auto` before the description for a non-interactive mode that answers its own questions. Use when the user asks to write a spec, specify a feature, or pin down requirements before planning.

items.name: /setup-gaia
items.description: Runs the single post-init onboarding. Detects the situation and runs only the owed phases; safe to re-run. --reconfigure re-asks the sandbox (an admin's answer also sets the team sandbox-recommendation, asked on its own only when that answer cannot), isolation-policy, squash-only-merge, and statusline decisions.

items.name: file-tech-debt
items.description: Files a new tech-debt GitHub issue for an out-of-scope code-review finding. Builds the dedup key, skips an open or declined-closed match, else creates the labeled issue and touches the debt-count sentinel. Trigger on asks like "file a tech-debt issue", "record this as tech-debt", "file this finding as debt". Do NOT trigger on draining, fixing, listing, or prioritizing existing debt (that's `/gaia-debt`), nor on general "clean up the code" or "fix this bug" asks that aren't about filing a new tracked issue.

items.name: gaia-wiki
items.description: Runs GAIA wiki maintenance (sync, consolidate, lint with fixes) in one command and lands it as one commit and PR. Trigger on `/gaia-wiki` or natural-language asks like "sync the wiki", "run wiki maintenance", "consolidate the wiki", or "lint the wiki".

items.name: naming-conventions
items.description: Applies descriptive, self-documenting naming in any language (TypeScript, bash, workflow YAML, Dockerfiles). Use this skill whenever naming or renaming an identifier, variable, constant, function, parameter, env var, workflow job, or Dockerfile ARG/ENV, or reviewing names for vagueness, abbreviations, or redundant type noise.

items.name: release-notes
items.description: Maintainer-only. Translates a version's GAIA CHANGELOG entries into plain-language public release notes for the marketing site (gaiareact.com), writing a release-data `.ts` file under `../website/src/pages/changelog/releases/` plus an editorial-decisions report for human review. Use when the maintainer wants the public notes for a version ("write release notes", "what's new on the site for v1.5.0"), right after cutting a release, or to backfill a historical `## [x.y.z]` block. Not for editing `CHANGELOG.md` or cutting a release (`/gaia-release`).

items.name: tdd
items.description: Runs test-driven development with a red-green-refactor loop. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs using TDD, mentions "red-green-refactor", wants integration tests, or asks for test-first development.

items.name: update-deps
items.description: Remediates dependencies in place of Dependabot version and security updates. Discovers outdated packages and open security advisories, resolves advisories (in-range refresh, chain-head bump, security-floor override, or alert dismissal), audits overrides, applies migrations for major bumps, and runs the quality gate. Trigger when the user clicks the statusline `📦 /update-deps` indicator or asks "update dependencies", "bump deps", "run dependabot", "fix Dependabot alerts", "fix security advisories".

items.name: update-gaia
items.description: Pulls the latest GAIA release into this project without clobbering customizations, with a three-way merge per file using .gaia/manifest.json classes. Trigger when the user clicks the statusline `🚀 /update-gaia` indicator or asks "update GAIA", "pull the latest GAIA", "apply the new GAIA release".

items.name: a11y-fixes
items.description: Resolves axe-core accessibility violations reported by a story under Vitest (addon-a11y), Playwright (.playwright/a11y.ts), or the code-audit-frontend agent's a11y bucket, with fix patterns for the common violations and a fix-then-verify loop for the rest. Trigger on any axe rule id appearing in test output.

items.name: eslint-fixes
items.description: Resolves the ESLint errors and warnings this project's lint config reports, including autofix conflicts. Use when fixing lint failures, ESLint-reported issues, or an autofix that fights another rule.

items.name: gaia-react-perf
items.description: Diagnoses React render performance by driving a micro-interaction, capturing real renders, and surfacing memo-defeating reference instability with a recommended structural fix. Measure-only, it emits a diagnosis and does not auto-fix. Trigger on `/gaia-react-perf` or natural-language asks like "profile renders", "measure renders", "why is X re-rendering", or "diagnose render performance". Do NOT trigger on vague "feels slow", "janky", or "optimize my app" (react-doctor's `scan` mode covers those).

items.name: new-component
items.description: Scaffolds a new React component with its Storybook story, which is the component's test. Use this skill whenever the user asks to "create a component", "make a button", "scaffold a card", "add a new component", or asks for a new file under `app/components/` following the project's component pattern (kebab-case folder, index.tsx, tests/), or asks for a component a shadcn registry item already provides (dialog, tabs, popover, and so on).

items.name: new-hook
items.description: Scaffolds a new custom React hook with a Vitest browser-mode test file. Use this skill whenever the user asks to "create a hook", "make a useFoo hook", "scaffold a custom React hook", "add a hook under app/hooks", or describes a piece of reusable React state/effect logic that warrants extraction into a named `use*` hook.

items.name: new-route
items.description: Scaffolds a new route with its page component, page story, and optional i18n keys. Use this skill whenever the user asks to "create a route", "add a new page", "scaffold /dashboard", "wire up a new route under _public or _session", or anything that implies adding a file under `app/routes/` with a matching `app/pages/{name}/` folder.

items.name: new-service
items.description: Scaffolds a new API service with request functions, Zod schemas, URL constants, optional TanStack Query options, and optional MSW mock handlers. Use this skill whenever the user asks to "add a service", "create the projects API", "wire up CRUD for users", or anything implying a new service folder under `app/services/` (`app/services/gaia/{name}/` until the `gaia/` folder is renamed) with parsers/types/requests + matching `test/mocks/{name}/` collections.

items.name: playwright-cli
items.description: Automate browser interactions, test web pages and work with Playwright tests.

items.name: react-code
items.description: Applies GAIA's patterns and conventions for writing and editing React components and hooks. Use this skill whenever writing or reviewing React components, hooks, or event handlers, or deciding on component extraction. Also trigger when deciding whether a manual memo or "use no memo" is justified under React Compiler, debugging stale closures or infinite re-renders, weighing a new dependency against a web-platform API or a hand-rolled primitive, choosing a React 19 idiom, or reaching for React's form Actions instead of React Router's form handling.

items.name: skeleton-loaders
items.description: Builds skeleton loading states that are pixel-perfect matches of real content. Use this skill whenever adding loading states to components, building skeletons for async data, handling pending loader states in route transitions, or implementing the shimmer animation pattern. Also trigger when the user asks about preventing layout shift during data fetching.

items.name: tailwind
items.description: Applies GAIA's patterns and conventions for all Tailwind styling. Use this skill whenever writing Tailwind class names, combining classes with `cn`, writing conditional classes, or building component variants. Also trigger when the user asks about custom values, defining @theme tokens or CSS variables, naming color/spacing tokens, rem vs px, responsive breakpoints, or avoiding template literal class strings.

items.name: tdd-react
items.description: Provides the React testing reference for the tdd skill. Covers test layers, the three Vitest projects, Storybook stories with play functions as component tests, vitest-browser-react hook tests, MSW, and Playwright patterns for the frontend package. Use when writing or reviewing tests under frontend/ as part of a red-green-refactor loop, choosing a test layer, mocking HTTP, or testing a component, hook, or service.

items.name: typescript
items.description: Applies GAIA's patterns and conventions for all TypeScript code. Use this skill whenever writing or reviewing TypeScript, typing exports, choosing between type and interface, using Zod schemas, defining a constant list, union type, or lookup map that other code shares, structuring function parameters, or enforcing code patterns like avoiding switch statements and enums.

items.description: Dispatched only by the audit loop as the workflow-YAML member of the Code Audit Team: read-only audit for supply-chain, injection, permission and secret defects. Never invoked directly.

items.description: Maintainer-only audit of the framework Node/CLI TypeScript, its render templates and test snapshots, and the CLI build/config surface the roster grants it: correctness, error handling, filesystem/IO safety, Zod schema fitness, shell/gh injection safety, and build-script/dependency/compiler-config safety. Read-only: reports findings and gates its marker; edits no tracked file. One member of the Code Audit Team gate.

items.name: code-audit-maintainer-shell
items.description: Maintainer-only audit of framework bash and the bats suites guarding it: quoting/portability correctness and conditional hook-contract and bats-suite lenses. Read-only: reports findings and gates its marker; edits no tracked file. One member of the Code Audit Team gate.
